context.problem_statement: Estimate price elasticity of demand using OLS regression on sales data. Use a log-log model: ln(quantity) = alpha + beta * ln(price) + gamma * ln(competitor_price) + epsilon. The coefficient beta is the own-price elasticity of demand and gamma is the cross-price elasticity. Fit the model using statsmodels OLS. Report: (1) own-price elasticity with confidence interval, (2) cross-price elasticity, (3) R-squared, (4) whether demand is elastic (|beta| > 1) or inelastic. Also compute the optimal price that maximizes revenue (P* = P / (1 + 1/beta) for elastic demand).
context.expert_knowledge: In log-log regression, coefficients directly represent elasticities. Own-price elasticity < -1: elastic demand (price cut increases revenue). Own-price elasticity between -1 and 0: inelastic demand. Cross-price elasticity > 0: substitute goods. Revenue-maximizing price derived from first-order condition. Use np.log for transformation and handle potential multicollinearity.
